speaker: Doctor
text:
Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a pruritic rash on your bilateral upper extremities; tell me, when did this rash first appear and how has the itchiness affected your daily life?

REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count (CBC)
REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Tests (LFTs)

speaker: Doctor
text: The CBC and liver function tests are normal. To narrow this down, were there any new soaps, detergents, or hobbies like gardening or handling animals involved in the week before the rash started?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient complains of a pruritic rash on both upper extremities that has been present for 5 months. She notes that the rash occasionally worsens but has not completely resolved at any point. She denies any recent illnesses and mentions that she has not started any new medications or come into contact with any new substances that she is aware of.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The rash has persisted for five months without resolution, and you've ruled out new allergens or recent illnesses. Given the chronic duration and bilateral distribution, have you noticed if the itchiness is worse at night or if the lesions appear as small bumps or blisters?

REQUEST TEST: Skin_Biopsy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Skin_Biopsy: Intraepidermal accumulation of edematous fluid and widening of intercellular spaces between keratinocytes.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The skin biopsy showing intraepidermal edema and widened intercellular spaces is highly characteristic of spongiosis. To confirm the specific cause, have you noticed any family members or household pets with similar skin issues, and does the rash spread to your trunk or other body parts?

REQUEST IMAGES: Dermoscopy

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pruritic rash on the bilateral upper extremities. I also have No fever, No joint pains, No recent illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Spongiotic Dermatitis (likely chronic allergic contact dermatitis or atopic dermatitis). The biopsy confirmed spongiosis, the clinical presentation fits a chronic pruritic rash on the upper extremities, and there are no signs of systemic infection or other major dermatological conditions like scabies or drug eruption.
